You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Oil Nears $100 as US Stocks Retreat; Intel Surges 9%; Apple’s Event Brings Foldable iPhone Questions into Focus (September 9, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Gasoline price expectations rise as the CPI release approaches
The New York Fed’s la test Survey of Consumer Expectations showed that one -year inflation expectations held at 3.6% in August. Three-year expectations eased to 3.2%, while five-year expectations remained at 3.0%.
Expected gasoline price growth over the next year increased by 1.7 percentage points to 4.6%, bringing energy costs back into focus.
US August PPI and CPI are scheduled for September 10 and 11, respectively, at 20:30 Beijing time, providing fresh evidence ahead of next week’s Federal Reserve meeting.
Market Impact : Overall inflation expectations have not risen across the board, but energy pressures are building. Sticky core inflation could keep technology stocks and crypto assets under valuation pressure through higher rate expectations. Cooler data would provide a clearer basis for a recovery in risk appetite.
International Commodities
US–Iran tensions spread to tankers, increasing energy supply risks
US Central Command said American forces destroyed five Iranian crude oil transport vessels on September 8.
Iran warned that tankers at ports in Kuwait and Bahrain could become targets and urged crews to evacuate.
With the conflict extending to energy transportation, oil supply and shipping security have become central market concerns.
Market Impact : Higher oil prices raise transportation and manufacturing costs and complicate disinflation. Energy producers may benefit from price support, while airlines, consumer businesses and other cost-sensitive industries face margin pressure. Gold must also contend with interest-rate expectations, so safe-haven demand does not automatically translate into higher prices.
Macroeconomic Policy
Expanded Treasury buybacks take effect today
The US Treasury previously announced that the maximum size of individual liquidity-support buybacks for nominal securities in the 10–20-year and 20–30-year sectors would rise from $2 billion to at least $4 billion, effective September 9.
A preliminary list of eligible securities for the next 10–20-year operation is due at 23:00 Beijing time tonight. Markets will also watch the announced maximum purchase amount.
The corresponding operation is scheduled for September 11, from 01:40 to 02:00 Beijing time. The announcement and execution fall on different dates.
Market Impact : Buybacks can improve liquidity in selected outstanding Treasuries, but they do not constitute a Federal Reserve rate cut. Equity investors will watch whether long-term yields ease and financing conditions improve for capital-intensive businesses such as AI infrastructure.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot gold : Approximately $4,349.23 per ounce.
Spot silver : Approximately $65.85 per ounce.
WTI crude oil futures : Approximately $94.65 per barrel, October 2026 contract.
Brent crude oil futures : Approximately $99.46 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approximately 98.78.
Driver Analysis : Brent is approaching $100, with energy transportation risks central to the oil trade. Gold remains below $4,400 as safe-haven demand competes with interest-rate pressure. Tonight’s Treasury buyback announcement and subsequent US inflation releases will remain important for currencies, precious metals and risk assets.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 78,759.81 USDT , down 0.66% over 24 hours.
ETH : Approximately 2,495.76 USDT, up 0.11% over 24 hours.
Total cryptocurrency market capitalization : Approximately $2.78 trillion.
Driver Analysis : BTC remains below 79,000 USDT, while ETH trades around 2,500 USDT and has modestly outperformed BTC over the past 24 hours. Oil and interest-rate expectations create external pressure, but the divergence between the two assets does not establish a broad crypto rebound. Near-term attention remains on risk appetite around US inflation data and the persistence of corporate and fund demand.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones Industrial Average : Closed at 52,786.07, down 1.18%.
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,673.52, down 0.58%.
Nasdaq Composite : Closed at 26,421.41, down 0.32%.
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $225.73, down 2.01%.
AAPL : $316.22, down 1.17%.
MSFT : $493.95, down 1.15%.
GOOGL : $338.36, down 0.03%.
AMZN : $256.97, down 0.60%.
META : $613.48, down 0.53%.
TSLA : $368.16, up 3.98%.
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : Using Alphabet’s Class A shares, one of the seven giants rose and six declined. Tesla led with a rebound, while Nvidia posted the largest decline; Apple and Microsoft both lost more than 1%. Higher oil prices and rate-hike concerns weighed on the broader market, even as selected chip , optical networking and AI cloud stocks advanced. AI demand headlines did not produce a broad megacap rally. Apple’s event is an important catalyst for the next session.
Sector Movers Observation
Semiconductors: CPU pricing expectations and AI demand provide catalysts
[...]
Drivers : Amazon and Qualcomm announced collaboration on AI inference chips and advanced optical connectivity, adding a fresh industry signal for data-center bandwidth upgrades. The agreement reinforces demand expectations, while its contribution to individual suppliers’ orders requires further disclosure.
[...]
3. Apple (AAPL) - Shares ease before the event as foldable pricing and upgrade demand face scrutiny
[...]
Event Overview : Apple fell 1.17% on September 8, closing at $316.22. Its special event is scheduled for September 10 at 01:00 Beijing time. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Apple had discussed a $2,199 starting price for its foldable iPhone amid memory cost pressures. Final pricing has not been announced.
[...]

The transaction is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions, with a focus on expanding USDC ’s practical payment reach.
